topic: Electrical Circuit: Series and Parallel Connections
key_concepts: An electric circuit is a closed loop through which current flows.
A continuous flow of electrons requires a complete circuit with no gaps.
Electric circuits have at least a voltage source, conducting wires, and loads.
An electrical switch can open or close a circuit to stop or allow current.
In a series circuit, current flows along only one pathway.
In a series circuit, total resistance is the sum of all individual resistances.
In a series circuit, the voltage source equals the sum of the voltages across each load.
In a series circuit, current is constant across each load.
If one bulb burns out in a series circuit, the other bulbs will not work.
Series circuits are commonly used in Christmas lights.
In a parallel circuit, current flows along more than one pathway.
Home appliances and light bulbs are usually connected in parallel.
